top.title: Patrick Mahomes Ended a TD Drought as Chiefs Beat The Falcons
top.description: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs had quite a day on Sunday. With Mahomes leading the attack, Kansas City took the Atlanta Falcons to the woodshed, showing the NFC South team what a real Super Bowl contender looks like. Mahomes had a game to remember against Atlanta, which struggled all game long to find a way to slow down the Chiefs at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. The three-time Super Bowl champion quarterback threw not just one, not two, not three, not four but five touchdowns with zero interceptions on 22/35 pass completions. Mahomes was also well protected, as he was sacked just once for a loss of nine yards. Even without star running back Kenneth Walker III , who was ruled out before the game with an injury, Kansas City’s attack overpowered the host team. Emmett Johnson filled in nicely for Walker, with the rookie running back burning rubber for 101 rushing yards on 22 carries, while also adding 70 receiving yards and two scores on six receptions and seven targets. top.title: How Mizzou basketball woke up Jason Crowe Jr., pulled off comeback vs Marquette
top.description: CHICAGO — Jason Crowe Jr. was trying to pull a fast one on his head coach. With 13 minutes, 24 seconds left on the gameclock, after riding the bench for the previous four minutes while Missouri basketball tried to dig itself out of a double-digit hole, Crowe tried to slip past Dennis Gates while the coach was making substitutions. Gates, even with his team trailing by six points, was having nothing of the sort from his star freshman point guard. The head coach grabbed Crowe’s arm and sent him back to his seat. Crowe sat there for another two minutes. “He knew I called somebody else. His little behind wanted to get back in the game. He thought I was going to let him go, and I pulled him back. He wanted to get back in the game, but he needed to watch some things,” Gates said. … “He's just ready to play. He looks at me with little puppy dog eyes when I look down. … I pointed at one person, gave him the nod, and he just ran trying to get an opportunity to get back in the game.” Crowe’s time came, and he didn’t waste it. “That's his way of saying, ‘Coach, I'm ready to go,’” Gates said. Missouri basketball staged a remarkable comeback win over Marquette on Sunday at United Center, beating the Golden Eagles 69-64 after looking down and out for most of the neutral-site contest. More: Mizzou basketball erases big deficit, defeats Marquette as Crowe closes strong The Tigers trailed the Golden Eagles by 11 points in the second half. But they’ve got a five-star freshman to help with sticky situations like that. Crowe went from lethargic to lethal in the game’s closing stretch. One catch-and-shoot 3-point shot and, with 49 seconds remaining, a turn-and-shoot triple that gave the Tigers the lead for good. A contested mid-ranger. A backdoor cut into a layup, and-1. Nowhere was safe from the free-scoring freshman once he turned it on. He finished with 17 points. Of those, 13 came in the final six minutes and 30 seconds of the game. Quite the turnaround. Crowe opened the game 1-of-8 from the field. He had six turnovers. That bought him a sideline seat. “He was bulls—ing early, man. I told him that. At the end of the day, I'm not gonna sugarcoat it with him,” Gates said. “He was BSing, and we needed him to step up, grow up in-game, stop looking for whistles. And once he stopped looking for a referee to rescue him, he became a participant with his team, and he focused up and made the big plays that we knew he could make for us.” That, like Mizzou’s outstanding offensive burst to close the game after a grizzly 24 turnovers, came from somewhere in the general vicinity of nowhere. At the mention of the number ‘24’ postgame, Crowe closed his eyes and mouthed an F-word we can’t print. Indeed. Twenty-four turnovers is the most in any game since Gates has arrived in Columbia. The Tigers matched the previous high of Gates’ tenure, which was 21 in a December 2022 loss to Kansas, when there were more than seven minutes left in the game. And that was hardly the only issue. top.title: Fairbanks boys soccer rolls to OHSAA Division V state championship
top.description: In a showdown of two first-time boys soccer state finalists , central Ohio’s representative got its championship. Fairbanks thoroughly dominated the Division V final Nov. 15 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field , getting goals from its top two offensive threats – sophomore forward Ty Schroeder and senior midfielder Kaden Procuniar – in a 4-0 win over Creston Norwayne that did not always feel that close. Fairbanks (22-2), just a year removed from its first district and regional titles, had the first 14 shots of the game and ultimately outshot Norwayne 28-2. Schroeder scored his team-leading 34th goal in the bottom center of the net with 32:15 left on the Panthers’ 13th shot of the game. Three minutes later, Procuniar netted his 11th goal of the year. He also finished with 21 assists. Senior forward Nolan Baker added the final two goals 30 seconds apart with less than seven minutes to go. Fairbanks, the first Union County program to win a state title, finished the season on a 14-game winning streak. The Panthers outscored their opponents 90-12. Norwayne (17-5-1) did not muster a shot until the 49th minute, when Lysander Bauman’s try was stopped by senior goalie Drew Sorg. That was Sorg’s only save of the game. Norwayne’s Garrett Ponting stopped seven shots. This story will be updated . High school sports reporter Dave Purpura can be reached at dpurpura@dispatch.com and at @dp_dispatch on X. top.title: ‘Ultimate pro since day one’… Dianna Russini praises NFL star after ’emotional’ postgame interview
top.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Returning NFL insider Dianna Russini has paid tribute to the man behind the biggest story in the league in Week 10 – Kirk Cousins. With the Minnesota Vikings’ season at risk of collapse, the team made an SOS trade for their former quarterback Kirk Cousins at the deadline, sending a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders. Cousins made a winning return to the Vikings – leading the team to a 30-10 win over NFC North rivals the Green Bay Packers. The 38-year-old quarterback fought back tears in his postgame interview, expressing his happiness at making a successful return to the team. He was praised by NFL personality Dianna Russini, who wrote on X: “Kirk has been the ultimate pro since day one in the league. “Seeing him get emotional after that win tells you everything about what this game still means to him. Great story.” What Kirk Cousins said after Vikings win Kirk Cousins was relieved to get the road win at Lambeau Field, and reminded the world why this game was a deeply personal one – as it was where his Vikings career came to an end. He said: “It was emotional coming to the stadium. Three years ago, tearing my Achilles here, it’s been a tough three years and I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today. “Grateful for my teammates and what they did today to make this outcome possible. It’s been a tough three years.” He added of his Vikings comeback: “There’s more to this story being written.” The victory takes the Vikings to 7-2, stopping a two-game losing streak. And in the process, it was the most dangerous the team has looked all year. Nobody would begrudge Cousins his moment. top.title: Mizzou women’s basketball holds off Lindenwood, improves to 5-0
top.description: Lindenwood opened its trip to Mizzou Arena with a 5-0 run. But the Tigers shut down any chance of an upset, using an 11-2 sprint of its own to bury the Lions. Mizzou held the lead the rest of the way, downing Lindenwood 79-63 and improving to 5-0 on the season. Both teams had the offense rolling early, but the Tigers held a 25-20 edge at the end of the first quarter. The Tigers were extremely efficient in the quarter, shooting 62.5% from the field and 50% from 3. Abbey Schreacke hit back-to-back 3-pointers for six early points. Khloe Ford also recorded six points in the opening frame. But Grace Slaughter led all scorers with nine points, shooting 4-5 from the field and a perfect 1-1 from three while playing all 10 minutes. From there, Lindenwood never got any closer. Mizzou started the second quarter on an 8-3 run, extending the lead out to 10. The Lions gave themselves a chance with less than three minutes to go in the fourth quarter, cutting the deficit down to nine. But the Tigers squashed any dreams of a comeback, holding their opponents scoreless for the final 2:44 of the game. “We went a few stretches offensively without scoring, but to me, the defense is what kept us ahead and kept us in charge of the game,” Mizzou coach Kellie Harper said. Slaughter added another six points in the fourth quarter, becoming a key contributor at both the start and end of the win. She led the team with 21 points, grabbing seven rebounds while shooting 8-14 from the field and 2-5 on 3-pointers. “I think our coaches really encourage us to rim run, play fast,” Slaughter said. “Our guards do a great job of hitting us in transition, and it is a lot of fun to play fast … they do a great job of helping me be in positions where I can be versatile, whether that’s on the perimeter shooting 3s or being able to find a mismatch inside and get a post up.” Slaughter moved into 10th place on the all-time scoring list, now up to 1,552 for her career. Next up is ninth-place Evan Unrau at 1,597. I’d expect Slaughter to catch her sometime within the next three games. “I’m just really thankful to get to play for Mizzou, but then on top of that, just play for a team that really cares for each other and a coaching staff that really pours into us and really helps us be successful on and off the court,” Slaughter said. “I wouldn’t be here if it weren’t for them.” Another key contribution came from Neveah Caffey, who scored 12 points and totalled a career-high seven assists. San Francisco’s interest in Engram reflected a need that extended beyond its wide receiver room. The 49ers were looking for dependable pass catchers who could help quarterback Brock Purdy while injuries affected the team’s offensive options. A tight end capable of working across the formation would have offered another way to create mismatches and keep the passing attack productive. top.title: England stun world champions Spain in one of their greatest victories
top.description: Anthony Gordon (from left), Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers celebrate a historic victory - Uefa via Getty Images/David Ramos Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege and a fight. This was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup trophy and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action. This was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford . So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and lunged with astonishing effect in the 84th minute to block a Nico Williams shot. Trafford again! 👊🏻An excellent double save from the Leeds United keeper 🙌 https://t.co/L27oQFQO1J — ITV Football (@itvfootball) November 15, 2026 This was a performance good enough to win a World Cup final, never mind Nations League Group A3 – just a shame England neglected to get to that World Cup final in the summer. The fight in question was at half-time as the players came off and White and Fabián Ruiz first tangled and others dived in. There was so much to admire. England began the night testing Spain’s first-phase passing to breaking point. They began the second half counter-attacking Spain for two goals from Ezri Konsa and White. Then after Elliot Anderson’s red card, this was a different England. With Trafford in inspired form, they held off the relentless Spain for long enough. Harry Kane scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and was replaced before the end so that Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy could give the midfield one more lease of life. By the end, the excitement meant that Kane was unable to take his seat on the bench, and he stood alongside Tuchel in the technical area, cajoling and advising. England have beaten Spain on Spanish territory in recent times, but it was the nature of this performance, its many qualities when the moment required them, that made it so significant. top.description: Mirra Andreeva is the third teenager to win the WTA Finals singles trophy on debut at the tournament [Getty Images] For Mirra Andreeva, the thought of her first WTA Finals singles campaign was so stressful that it gave her "a little breakdown" in a practice session before the tournament. The 19-year-old may have been nervous on arrival at Indian Wells, but she leaves California as the champion, having been the standout player of the week. The French Open winner produced a hard-fought 7-5 6-3 victory over Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final to become the youngest champion of the event in 22 years. The Russian has now risen to second in the world rankings - and she will start the 2027 season just 293 points behind top-ranked Elena Rybakina. Andreeva did not drop a set on her way to the title and lost only 26 games across her five matches. She raised her arms in celebration after beating Svitolina before racing to celebrate with her team, which includes 1994 Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez. "I am super thankful to my team for pushing me to my limits, for forcing me to do stuff when I don't want to do anything," Andreeva said. "Thanks for fighting with me, thanks for forcing me to do everything that I have to do and not asking any questions!" As well as £2.55m in prize money, Andreeva also won a custom purple Mercedes - and joked she was happy to remain a "passenger princess" until she passed her test. Andreeva thanks herself again after stellar season Mirra Andreeva is the youngest WTA Finals champion since a 17-year-old Maria Sharapova in 2004 [Getty Images] One of the most notable parts of Andreeva's performance has been her increased maturity. In March, she swore at the Indian Wells crowd after suffering an early defeat in the venue's WTA Tour tournament, and she has struggled to control her emotions on court in the past. However, she showed little sign of that during this tournament. Against Svitolina, one of the grittiest players on the women's tour, she lost a break lead three times across the two sets. Each time, she reset admirably, upping her aggression on her backhand in particular to put pressure back on her opponent. After losing serve in a mammoth nine-minute game in the second set, Andreeva marched back to her chair and then broke Svitolina from 40-0 down in the next game to stay in front. While her serve was not at its best, Andreeva still saved nine of the 12 break points she faced and hit 19 winners to Svitolina's 10. "This fighting mindset helped me to get more brave and aggressive in the important moments," Andreeva told Sky Sports. "This is just a dream. nigeria.title: Diabetes: CAPPA urges FG, states to impose 20% sugary drinks tax, reform food policies
nigeria.description: By Chioma Obinna On this day World Diabetes Day, the Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) on Saturday called on the Federal Government and state governments to urgently reform Nigeria’s food policies, impose a minimum 20 per cent tax on sugar-sweetened beverages and tighten regulations on unhealthy food products to curb the rising burden of diabetes. The organisation warned that efforts to tackle the disease would yield limited results if government focused on screening and treatment while allowing aggressive marketing, widespread availability and affordability of ultra-processed foods and sugary drinks to continue unchecked. Making the call in a message to mark the 2026 World Diabetes Day, marked November 14, with the theme, “Early Action on Diabetes”, CAPPA said Nigeria faced an escalating diabetes crisis that required decisive government intervention beyond public awareness and individual lifestyle changes. According to the organisation, Nigeria has the highest number of adults aged 20 to 79 living with diabetes in Africa, while nearly three in four adults with diabetes across the continent remain undiagnosed. It warned that delayed diagnosis exposes millions of Nigerians to potentially life-threatening complications, including kidney failure, blindness, stroke and amputations. CAPPA also raised the alarm over the financial burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases, citing an estimated N1.92 trillion annual out-of-pocket expenditure by Nigerian households on their treatment. Executive Director of CAPPA, Akinbode Oluwafemi, said diabetes prevention should not be reduced to individual discipline when commercial interests and unhealthy food environments increasingly shape people’s dietary choices. He said: “We cannot keep telling Nigerians to eat healthily while allowing unhealthy food and beverages to dominate our markets, schools, advertisements and public spaces. “Early action on diabetes must begin with enacting and implementing strong regulatory policies that make healthy choices possible, affordable and accessible, not simply with advising people to change their dietary behaviour.” The organisation cited its 2025 report, Junk On Our Plates, which documented aggressive marketing of ultra-processed foods and beverages high in sugar and sodium across seven Nigerian states. It said the report exposed the targeting of children, young people and low-income communities through advertising, celebrity endorsements, misleading nutrition labels and cultural imagery designed to promote unhealthy products. To reverse the trend, CAPPA outlined five major policy interventions, beginning with the conclusion and enforcement of the proposed Sugar-Sweetened Beverage (SSB) tax. It urged the House of Representatives and the Federal Executive to complete legislative action following the Senate’s passage of the tax review bill earlier this year. nigeria.title: Igbokoda Crash: NAF recovers black box, holds memorial November 26
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has confirmed the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) from the site of the October 5 aircraft crash at Igbokoda, Ondo State, announcing plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony for the victims on November 26. The ceremony will take place at the National Military Cemetery, Abuja, in honour of the personnel and other victims who lost their lives in the NAF 931 aircraft accident. NAF Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the event would provide an opportunity for bereaved families, colleagues, friends and members of the Air Force community to pay their last respects. He said the ceremony would also serve as a formal expression of the Service’s respect and remembrance for those who died in the incident. On the recovery of the aircraft’s black box, Ejodame said the CVR, alongside other aircraft fragments and relevant evidence, had been retrieved from the crash site. He explained that data recovered from the voice recorder was being analysed and was expected to contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident. According to him, the investigation is progressing in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA). The Air Force reiterated its commitment to ensuring that the investigation was conducted in accordance with the highest standards of professionalism, transparency, accountability and responsibility, while supporting the independent technical processes required to establish the cause of the crash. Ejodame further disclosed that recovery operations had yielded several human remains and aircraft fragments, while the identification process for the recovered remains was ongoing. He said the operation had been particularly challenging because of the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth to which some of the aircraft wreckage had penetrated the ground. The NAF spokesman added that the Service was engaging relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery exercise and ensure appropriate remediation after its completion. He said the Air Force recognised the grief of the bereaved families and remained committed to providing them with sustained support throughout the difficult period. The Service also appreciated the cooperation of relevant agencies, host communities and other stakeholders who had continued to support the recovery and investigation efforts. The NAF assured the public of its commitment to a thorough investigation, responsible environmental management and the dignified remembrance of all those who lost their lives. Considered among the best midfielders in the history of the game, Xavi formed the core of a possession-dominant Barcelona side who won four Champions League titles. And that’s exciting. I always loved playing against teams who play like this.” Third in the group with only the top two reaching the quarter-finals, Germany will need to beat the Netherlands to give themselves a chance. “They’re a team who really come alive in European football,” Klopp said of the Netherlands. “It’s one of the fiercest rivalries in football. It’s a great honour for me.” Appointed in August, the Spaniard said he was beginning to understand the nature of the rivalry with Germany. “Now I can understand more because I’m here and I feel this kind of rivalry. In his press conference, Xavi deflected Klopp’s praise and said the Netherlands’ big win over Greece was down to his players. “It’s not Xavi-football. It’s all about the players. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. entertainment.title: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar Makes History as First Female Vice-Chancellor of UNIJOS
entertainment.description: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar, appointed as the 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor and first female Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jos. The University of Jos (UNIJOS) has officially appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the institution was established in 1971. Announced on Thursday, 12 November 2026 by the university’s Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent , during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council, the historic appointment sees Professor Lar succeed Professor Tanko Ishaya as she takes the helm of the Plateau State institution. Born in Langtang, Plateau State, Professor Lar is a distinguished Professor of Medical Microbiology whose career has been deeply woven into the fabric of UNIJOS for nearly four decades. After earning her Bachelor of Science degree in Microbiology from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1986, she joined the University of Jos in 1987 as a Graduate Assistant in the Department of Medical Microbiology. She later went on to earn her Master’s degree in Medical Microbiology in 1989 and her PhD in Medical Parasitology in 1998 from the University of Lagos, followed by postdoctoral training at the Institute of Human Virology, University of Maryland in the United States under the NIH-Fogarty Fellowship Programme. Rising steadily through the academic ranks, she became an Associate Professor in 2012 before attaining full professorship in October 2015. Over the years, she has built an impressive body of work with more than 40 scholarly publications focusing on infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS, malaria, antimicrobial resistance, and phytomedicine. Beyond the lecture hall and laboratory, Professor Lar has also served in key administrative roles at UNIJOS—including Head of the Department of Microbiology and Director of Linkages and Collaborations—and previously served a six-month tenure as Acting Vice-Chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University (formerly the University of Abuja) following her appointment by President Bola Tinubu in February 2025. Alongside her academic and leadership credentials, Professor Lar is a recognised advocate for women’s empowerment, having received the He4She Certificate of Award for Women Empowerment Activism in 2019. As she begins her five-year single term as UNIJOS’s first female substantive Vice-Chancellor after 55 years, she brings nearly four decades of institutional experience to the university’s top seat. This is the conversation the Train The Trainers Summit (TTTS) Lagos Edition seeks to ignite when it convenes on Saturday, 28 November 2026, at the D’Podium International Event Centre, Aromire, Ikeja, off Adeniyi Jones, Lagos. entertainment.title: Team Nigeria Records Its Best-Ever Youth Olympic Gold Medal Haul at Dakar 2026
entertainment.description: Nigerian sprint champions Praise Tejiri Ugoh, Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo, and Gift Bright celebrate their historic gold medal victories at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Photo Credit: MakingOfChamps Team Nigeria delivered an unforgettable chapter at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal, wrapping up a historic multi-sport gathering that marked the first time an Olympic-branded event was ever hosted on African soil. Spanning across vibrant venues in Dakar, Diamniadio, and Saly, the Games brought together thousands of young athletes across 25 sports in a true celebration of youth culture, elite competition and unity. The grandeur of the international sporting festival kicked off with a breathtaking opening ceremony at the packed Abdoulaye Wade Stadium in Diamniadio. The night dazzled spectators with rich West African cultural displays, vibrant musical showcases, and a live performance by Nigerian music artist Ibquake , who brought incredible flair to the historic arena alongside global digital stars like Khaby Lame . Amidst the festive atmosphere, the Nigerian delegation walked with immense pride, led by sprint prodigy Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo carrying the national flag. Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo rejoices on the track wrapped in the green and white national flag after securing the women’s 100m gold. Photo Credit: MakingOfChamps/Instagram When the action shifted to the tracks at the Complexe Iba Mar Diop, Team Nigeria turned the athletics arena into a showcase of pure speed, finishing their campaign with a total of three medals—all of them gold. Fifteen-year-old Gift Bright set the blazing pace by conquering the men’s 100m final in a personal-best and Games-record time of 10.28 seconds, earning the distinction of becoming the first Nigerian men’s 100m champion at the Youth Olympics. Gift Bright powers down the track en route to winning the men’s 100m gold in a personal-best 10.28 seconds. Photo Credit: MakingOfChamps/Instagram Matching that stellar brilliance, flagbearer Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo blazed across the finish line in the women’s 100m final in 11.16 seconds, completing a phenomenal sprint double that crowned Nigeria as the first nation in Youth Olympic history to sweep both 100m titles at a single edition. The golden sweep was officially sealed by sixteen-year-old Praise Tejiri Ugoh , who stormed through the women’s 400m final in a personal-best time of 52.76 seconds to claim gold and become the first Nigerian to conquer the 400m distance at the Games. Praise Tejiri Ugoh claims gold for Nigeria on the podium following the women’s 400m final at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Photo Credit: MakingOfChamps/Instagram These remarkable achievements by Gift Bright, Rosemary Chigozie Nwankwo, and Praise Tejiri Ugoh not only surpassed Nigeria’s previous best tally of two gold medals from the inaugural Singapore 2010 Games, but also firmly established the country’s rising track stars as global names to watch. entertainment.title: Ramla Ali Wins IBF and WBO Titles to Become Somalia’s First Boxing World Champion
entertainment.description: Unified world champion Ramla Ali poses in the ring with her WBO and IBF super-bantamweight belts and her coaching team in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram British-Somali boxer and fashion model Ramla Ali is officially a unified world champion! On 8 November 2026 at the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, the 37-year-old athlete captured the vacant IBF and WBO super-bantamweight world titles after securing a split-decision victory over American contender Mikiah Kreps . During the ten-round bout, Ali dropped Kreps with a sharp right hand in the third round—the sole knockdown of the night—before two judges scored the contest 97–92 and 96–93 in her favour, against one scorecard of 98–91 for Kreps. With this triumph, Ali became Somalia’s first-ever professional boxing world champion and a unified titleholder in one unforgettable night. Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, she fled the civil war as a child with her family and grew up in East London, initially taking up boxing in secret as a teenager before turning it into a life-changing calling. Ramla Ali makes her ring walk behind the Somali and British flags ahead of her super-bantamweight world title fight in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Her remarkable journey from refugee to Olympic athlete and champion is also the subject of the biographical feature film In the Shadows. Directed by Anthony Wonke , the film premiered at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2026 before opening in UK and Irish cinemas on 30 October—just over a week before she lifted her world title belts in Texas. BAFTA-winning Top Boy actress Jasmine Jobson stars as Ali alongside Peaky Blinders actor Finn Cole as her husband and former coach, Richard Moore , with both Ali and Moore serving as executive producers on the project. This championship milestone builds on a string of barrier-breaking firsts across sports, cinema, and fashion. Long before her title win in Arlington, Ali made history as the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title, the first boxer to win an international gold medal while representing Somalia, and the first boxer to represent Somalia on the Olympic stage when she competed in the women’s featherweight division at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics. Ramla Ali celebrates in the ring as the referee raises her hand following her split-decision victory over Mikiah Kreps on 8 November 2026. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Away from the ring, she has carved out an equally notable space in global luxury fashion. Ali has graced the covers of British Vogue, Elle UK, Harper’s Bazaar Arabia, and Grazia UK, served as a brand ambassador for Cartier and Dior, and made history as the first boxer to wear custom ring attire created by major fashion houses—including bespoke fight kits designed by Dior, Off-White, Versace, Alexander McQueen, and Burberry featuring the panther emblem from Somalia’s coat of arms. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. sports.description: Mirra Andreeva is the third teenager to win the WTA Finals singles trophy on debut at the tournament [Getty Images] For Mirra Andreeva, the thought of her first WTA Finals singles campaign was so stressful that it gave her "a little breakdown" in a practice session before the tournament. The 19-year-old may have been nervous on arrival at Indian Wells, but she leaves California as the champion, having been the standout player of the week. The French Open winner produced a hard-fought 7-5 6-3 victory over Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final to become the youngest champion of the event in 22 years. The Russian has now risen to second in the world rankings - and she will start the 2027 season just 293 points behind top-ranked Elena Rybakina. Andreeva did not drop a set on her way to the title and lost only 26 games across her five matches. She raised her arms in celebration after beating Svitolina before racing to celebrate with her team, which includes 1994 Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez. "I am super thankful to my team for pushing me to my limits, for forcing me to do stuff when I don't want to do anything," Andreeva said. "Thanks for fighting with me, thanks for forcing me to do everything that I have to do and not asking any questions!" As well as £2.55m in prize money, Andreeva also won a custom purple Mercedes - and joked she was happy to remain a "passenger princess" until she passed her test. Andreeva thanks herself again after stellar season Mirra Andreeva is the youngest WTA Finals champion since a 17-year-old Maria Sharapova in 2004 [Getty Images] One of the most notable parts of Andreeva's performance has been her increased maturity. In March, she swore at the Indian Wells crowd after suffering an early defeat in the venue's WTA Tour tournament, and she has struggled to control her emotions on court in the past. However, she showed little sign of that during this tournament. Against Svitolina, one of the grittiest players on the women's tour, she lost a break lead three times across the two sets. Each time, she reset admirably, upping her aggression on her backhand in particular to put pressure back on her opponent. After losing serve in a mammoth nine-minute game in the second set, Andreeva marched back to her chair and then broke Svitolina from 40-0 down in the next game to stay in front. While her serve was not at its best, Andreeva still saved nine of the 12 break points she faced and hit 19 winners to Svitolina's 10. "This fighting mindset helped me to get more brave and aggressive in the important moments," Andreeva told Sky Sports. "This is just a dream. I had a little breakdown in my practice just before Indian Wells because I was so stressed. "I didn't want to lose a match in the group. It's amazing." Andreeva had only won one of her six matches against top-10 players in 2026 coming into the tournament. She has beaten three top-10 players en route to the title, including a demolition of four-time major champion Aryna Sabalen

It's a perfect evening… in 1996 or 2026. The entire concept of "Space Jam" is so '90s that you swear you can hear Los Del Rio in the background mouthing, "Dale a tu cuerpo alegría, Macarena." In case you thought you hallucinated the whole thing, no, you didn't, as the Looney Tunes find themselves in quite the predicament in this live-action-animation hybrid. A bunch of aliens known as the Nerdlucks arrive on Earth to abduct the Tunes and take them back as attractions to the outer-space amusement park known as Moron Mountain (shockingly nobody has claimed that subreddit, so do your thing, Internet!). Being a wheeling-and-dealing wabbit, though, Bugs Bunny proposes a winner-takes-all basketball game between the Tunes and the tiny Nerdlucks. Unfortunately, the crafty aliens use their tech to steal the talent from ballers like Charles Barkley and Muggsy Bogues and turn themselves into the scary and skilled Monstars. So, Bugs and friends reach out to Michael Jordan, who recently switched from basketball to baseball, to help the Tune Squad win this intergalactic b-ball matchup and their freedom, because if anybody can do it, Air Jordan (Hare Jordan?) can. Oh, Bill Murray also shows up here a few times. Why? Because he can! (Image credit: Warner Bros. Pictures) "Space Jam" is a spin on the classic sci-fi trope of resolving high-stakes conflicts through sports. In 1975, "Death Race 2000" introduced a world where people drive like hooligans and bash into each other to get ahead and win races (ironically, this is the regular experience on any public road now). Yet "Space Jam" took this concept, cartoonified it for a family-friendly audience, and challenged the conflict resolution approaches of other alien invasion movies from 1996. While " Independence Day " saw the heroes trying to destroy the mothership and "Mars Attacks" featured humans running away from "Ack! science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
science.description: null On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) Why it mattered When the 300-foot telescope first debuted, it was not just the United States' largest radio observatory, but the largest such facility in the world. But its quick construction — just two years — led to it having to be significantly upgraded later. "In 1970, the 300-foot’s surface had become so warped from maintenance crews, snow, and its own weight that a new finer-meshed aluminum surface was installed," the website for the National Radio Astronomy Observatory reads. "A larger traveling feed was also installed at the prime focus." The collapse, however, was no one's fault. "Unforeseeable stress factors cracked a steel connector plate," wrote the NRAO. The Green Bank Telescope collapse left a mass of twisted debris behind. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) During its years of observations, the 300-foot telescope contirbuted to the discovery of dark matter and the realization that pulsars come from supernova explosions. "One of the most important products to come out of the 300-foot telescope was an all-sky survey of radio objects called the Green Bank 6cm Survey. Nearly every northern hemisphere radio object studied by any other telescope is from a catalog compiled using this telescope," reads the NRAO website. Want more space history? But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold. Next comes a dramatic nova explosion that causes the star to flare to 1,000 times its usual brightness before gradually settling down and repeating the cycle. Why is it so challenging to predict T. CrB's nova flare? "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon," Bradley Schaefer of the Louisiana State University Department of Physics and Astronomy told Space.com in an email. "Everyone is very confident on this. But we cannot make high-accuracy measures of the rate of gas falling onto the surface of the white dwarf, and we do not have a high accuracy measure of the trigger mass for the big hydrogen bomb." Schaefer continued. Historical observations reveal that the last nova eruption reached Earth in 1946, which places us well inside the window for another dramatic brightening of T. CrBb. However, the unpredictability of the white dwarf's feeding makes it difficult to pin down exactly when the explosion will become visible from Earth. An animation of T. CrB brightening. science.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
science.description: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year. On June 14, as it headed towards perihelion – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an astronomical unit) , 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life. On 31 May, the comet was languishing at magnitude +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes. By June 2, 220P was up to magnitude +8.23 and was technically visible for a short while in 10x50 binoculars from a dark site, prompting amateur astronomers and astrophotographers to chase down this rare event. By perihelion, the comet had faded back to magnitude +12, but more was to come. A second outburst began at the end of July, brightening from magnitude +14 on 28 July to magnitude 6.1 by 6 August. Telling the tale of a dirty snowball Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space. Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten. "We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. science.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
science.description: null Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three test flights to date. But it had never caught a Ship before; indeed, it had never even tried before Saturday. It's tougher and riskier to catch Ship; the upper stage flies much higher and faster than Super Heavy, so its return trip is much more more involved. Saturday was therefore a very big day for the company. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." The F light 15 mission plan gave us a sneak peek at the future: The double catch will be standard on operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will enable rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight of the megarocket, according to SpaceX. And the company is indeed planning on rapid reflight. Elon Musk has said that SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship launches per year by 2030, which works out to more than one liftoff every hour on average. Why such a mind-boggling cadence? Because SpaceX plans to build megaconstellations far larger than anything circling Earth today. For example, it wants its next-gen Starlink V3 broadband network to consist of 100,000 satellites . science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide on everything you need to observe and photograph the planets of the solar system, along with our picks of the top telescopes , cameras and lenses for exploring the night sky in 2026. science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972. science.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
science.description: null This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed. In more recent years, most notably 1999 , 2001 and 2002 , lesser Leonid displays of up to "only" a few thousand meteors per hour took place. Unfortunately, that's not likely to be the case this year. In fact, comparatively speaking, this is going to be a lean year for the Leonids chiefly because of the expected lack of any significant activity. Although the Leonids are one of the most famous of all the annual meteor displays, this year they're not likely to be very productive. It's probable they are going to be rather weak and there probably will be long stretches when not a single Leonid will be seen. I'll explain why in a moment. First, let's find out about this shower's lineage. What causes the Leonids? The Leonids are so named because the shower's radiant point, from where the meteors seem to fan out, is located within the constellation of Leo the Lion, from the backward question mark pattern of stars known as " The Sickle." The meteors are caused by the Tempel-Tuttle comet , which sweeps through the inner solar system every 33⅓ years. Each time the comet passes closest to the sun it leaves a "river of rubble" in its wake: a dense trail of dusty debris. A meteor storm becomes possible if the Earth were to score a direct hit on a fresh dust trail ejected by the comet over the past several centuries. The "lion's share" (no pun intended) of comet dust can be found just ahead and trailing behind Tempel-Tuttle. That comet last swept through the inner solar system in 1998. That's why spectacular meteor showers were seen in 1999, 2001 and 2002, with declining numbers thereafter. The most famous depiction of the 1833 Leonids, actually produced in 1888 for the Adventist book Bible Readings for the Home Circle . The engraving is by Adolf Vollmy based upon an original painting by the Swiss artist Karl Jauslin, that is in turn based on a first-person account of the 1833 storm by a minister, Joseph Harvey Waggoner on his way from Florida to New Orleans. science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

In many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication. But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. In fact, working out how to establish a dialogue with extraterrestrial visitors becomes the whole point of this powerful and heartbreaking story, as the fate of planet Earth hinges on the interpretation of a single noun. The film's journey to the big screen began when a screenwriter best known for his work on horror franchises such as "Final Destination", "A Nightmare on Elm Street" and "The Thing" read a short story in an online magazine. Eric Heisserer was so impressed by Ted Chiang's "Understand" that he bought himself a collection of the author's short stories. One in particular, the Nebula Award-winning "Story of Your Life", piqued his interest. "It had a very profound emotional effect on me," he reminisced to Deadline .
